title: Somatostatin Interneurons in Neurodegenerative Disease
thesis_question: Is loss or dysfunction of somatostatin-expressing (SST) interneurons a shared, causally important feature across neurodegenerative diseases? If so, which mechanisms (cell-intrinsic vulnerability, peptide/SSTR signaling, circuit dysregulation) drive it, how robust is the human and model evidence, and does it justify SST-targeted biomarkers and therapies?
audience: Neuroscientists and translational researchers in neurodegeneration, interneuron biology and circuit neuroscience (graduate level and above).

clusters.name: SST interneuron identity, connectivity and somatostatin receptor signaling
topics: Transcriptomic/morpho-electric SST subtypes (Martinotti, non-Martinotti, Sst-Chodl long-range, Patch-seq taxonomies)
Cortical, hippocampal (O-LM, HIPP, bistratified) and striatal SST/NPY/NOS cell types
Input/output connectivity: dendritic targeting, disinhibitory VIP->SST motifs, SST->PV
Somatostatin peptide processing and release; SSTR1-5 distribution, G-protein signaling, co-transmission with GABA

clusters.name: Selective vulnerability of SST interneurons in aging and neurodegeneration
topics: Age-related SST/peptide decline in cortex and hippocampus across species
Cell-intrinsic vulnerability: metabolic load, calcium handling, excitotoxicity, ER/oxidative stress, neurotrophin (BDNF) dependence
Hilar SST cell loss after injury/seizure as vulnerability model; cross-disease vulnerability comparisons

clusters.name: Alzheimer's disease: SST loss, amyloid-beta/neprilysin, tau and hyperexcitability
topics: Postmortem and model SST depletion in AD; SST-neprilysin regulation of Abeta degradation
SST-Abeta co-aggregation/binding, SSTR-dependent effects; tau propagation and SST cell vulnerability
Network hyperexcitability, subclinical seizures, and interneuron dysfunction in APP/tau models

clusters.name: Parkinson's disease and Lewy body dementias
topics: Cortical and CSF SST reductions in PD, PDD and DLB; alpha-synuclein pathology in interneurons
Striatal SST/NPY/NOS interneurons under dopamine depletion; L-DOPA dyskinesia
Cognitive impairment and SST in Lewy body disease

clusters.name: Huntington's disease and striatal SST interneurons
topics: Relative sparing vs dysfunction of striatal SST/NPY/NOS interneurons in HD
Mutant huntingtin effects on interneuron physiology; cortical SST changes in HD models and patients
Mechanisms of differential vulnerability (spiny projection neurons vs interneurons)

clusters.name: ALS, frontotemporal dementia and other neurodegenerative conditions
topics: Motor cortex SST interneurons and cortical hyperexcitability in ALS (SOD1, TDP-43, C9orf72 models)
Interneuron pathology in FTD/FTLD (tau, TDP-43, GRN, C9orf72)
Other conditions: prion disease, Down syndrome, multiple sclerosis cortical lesions, chronic traumatic encephalopathy, epilepsy-associated neurodegeneration

clusters.name: Circuit consequences: dendritic inhibition, oscillations, sleep and memory
topics: SST-mediated dendritic inhibition, plasticity gating, and loss-of-function effects on pyramidal integration
Theta/gamma/beta oscillations and SST contributions; oscillatory deficits in disease models
Slow-wave sleep, spindles and SST interneurons; sleep disruption in neurodegeneration
Memory encoding/consolidation dependent on SST cells (O-LM, engram regulation)

clusters.name: Human evidence: postmortem pathology, single-nucleus atlases and CSF somatostatin
topics: Postmortem SST immunoreactivity and cell counts across neurodegenerative diseases
Single-nucleus RNA-seq/spatial atlases (e.g., SEA-AD, ROSMAP) reporting SST subtype depletion
CSF somatostatin as a biomarker: diagnostic accuracy, longitudinal and cross-disease studies, assay issues

clusters.name: Therapeutic strategies targeting SST signaling and SST interneurons
topics: SSTR agonists (incl. SSTR2/SSTR4-selective), neprilysin up-regulation via SST, blood-brain barrier issues
Interneuron-targeted interventions: chemogenetic/optogenetic rescue, MGE progenitor transplantation, gene therapy
Neuromodulation: 40 Hz sensory/gamma entrainment, TMS/tDCS/DBS effects on interneuron function; antiseizure approaches (levetiracetam)

clusters.name: Conflicting evidence, model limitations and methodological caveats
topics: Contradictory findings on SST loss vs dysfunction; cell loss vs marker downregulation
Mouse model validity (transgenic overexpression artifacts, Sst-Cre line caveats), species differences
Postmortem confounds (agonal state, PMI), cohort heterogeneity, replication gaps

sections.title: Introduction
sections.scope_notes: Written last (Phase 11) and may cite only papers already used in body sections. It frames SST interneurons as a cell class that is vulnerable across diseases, states the central question, and previews the argument arc.

sections.title: SST Interneuron Identity: Transcriptomic Subtypes, Connectivity, and Somatostatin Receptor Signaling
sections.scope_notes: Foundation section. Covers transcriptomic subtypes, connectivity motifs and SSTR1-5 signaling, which later sections need to interpret disease findings.

sections.title: Selective Vulnerability of SST Interneurons in Aging and Neurodegeneration
sections.scope_notes: Cross-disease and aging vulnerability mechanisms; separates loss of SST cells from loss of the peptide or marker.

sections.title: Alzheimer's Disease: SST Loss, Amyloid-β and Neprilysin, Tau, and Network Hyperexcitability
sections.scope_notes: AD: SST depletion, SST-neprilysin-Abeta axis, tau, and hyperexcitability; weigh human vs model data.

sections.title: Parkinson's Disease and Lewy Body Dementias
sections.scope_notes: PD, PDD and DLB: cortical, striatal and CSF SST evidence; alpha-synuclein interactions.

sections.title: Huntington's Disease and Striatal SST Interneurons
sections.scope_notes: HD: why striatal SST/NPY/NOS interneurons are relatively spared, and evidence that they are nonetheless dysfunctional.

sections.title: ALS, Frontotemporal Dementia, and Other Neurodegenerative Conditions
sections.scope_notes: ALS, FTD and other conditions; keep scope to SST/interneuron-relevant evidence.

sections.title: Circuit Consequences: Dendritic Inhibition, Oscillations, Sleep, and Memory
sections.scope_notes: Circuit-level consequences: dendritic inhibition, oscillations, sleep, memory; bridge cellular findings to symptoms.

sections.title: Human Evidence: Postmortem Pathology, Single-Nucleus Atlases, and CSF Somatostatin as a Biomarker
sections.scope_notes: Human evidence synthesis: postmortem, snRNA-seq atlases, CSF SST biomarker performance.

sections.title: Therapeutic Strategies: Somatostatin Receptor Agonists, Interneuron-Targeted Interventions, and Neuromodulation
sections.scope_notes: Therapeutics: SSTR agonists, interneuron-targeted interventions and neuromodulation; translational status and failures.

sections.title: Conflicting Evidence, Model Limitations, and Open Questions
sections.scope_notes: Cross-cutting critical section: conflicting results, model limitations, open questions. Draws on conflicts flagged in every cluster.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.scope_notes: Written last (Phase 11) and may cite only existing papers. Synthesizes the thesis answer and sets priorities for future work.

evidence_parameters_rationale: User prompt asks for a 'comprehensive critical literature review' but specifies no per-cluster paper count, saturation language, snowballing, or bibliography floor; all four defaults applied per comprev-scoping parsing rules.

steps.title: Generate BibTeX
steps.description: Build the BibTeX from CrossRef for every cite key used. Output must be ASCII-only and deduplicated by DOI, followed by a contamination scan for keys or DOIs not in citation_key_map. Coordinator verifies: zero undefined keys, zero unused-but-claimed DOIs, ASCII check passes.

steps.title: Six-pass integration
steps.description: Run 6 passes over sections 02-11: transitions, cross-references, terminology (SST subtype nomenclature, SSTR naming), continuity, figure numbering via \ref{}, hygiene. Coordinator verifies: no broken refs, consistent terminology table, no new uncited claims introduced.

steps.title: Write section_01 Introduction and section_12 Conclusion
steps.description: Write both bookends after all body sections are complete. They may cite only papers already cited in the body. Coordinator verifies: every cite key in section_01/section_12 already appears in sections 02-11; titles match TOC verbatim; the thesis answer is consistent with section_11 caveats.

steps.title: Blinded bookend critique
steps.description: Critique the introduction and conclusion blind. Check every new claim-citation pair against the cited paper's source sentence. Coordinator verifies: MUST_FIX items resolved; no overclaiming beyond body evidence.

steps.title: Write Methods.md and architecture figure
steps.description: Render pipeline metadata (search strategy, evidence_parameters, paper counts, fulltext rates, validation outcomes) into Methods.md plus an architecture figure. Coordinator verifies: all counts are read from gate artifacts, not hand-entered.

steps.title: Assemble document
steps.description: Collect all section files, figures and notebooks, verify paths, build the LaTeX preamble and myst.yml TOC, and run the assertions. Coordinator verifies (Phase 14V): REVIEW_REQUEST_CAPTURED passes (no placeholders), all 12 sections present in TOC order, FORBIDDEN_LEXICON scan clean, build succeeds.

steps.title: Extract citation triples exhaustively
steps.description: Emit one (claim, cite key, DOI) triple per cite-key occurrence across the document, with no sampling. Coordinator verifies: triple count equals the total cite occurrence count.

steps.title: Deep-verify every triple (parallel shards)
steps.description: For every triple, run the 5-step check: DOI resolves → title matches → authors match → metadata matches → full-text claim support. No tiering. Coordinator verifies: every triple has a verdict; unverifiable items are flagged, never passed by default.

steps.title: Build fix requests
steps.description: For every triple not marked VERIFIED, build a fix request with ±10 lines of context. Coordinator verifies: one fix request per non-VERIFIED triple.

steps.title: Apply bib and text fixes (parallel)
steps.description: Apply the bibliography and text fixes for each request, replacing or removing unsupported citations and softening claims to what the sources say. Coordinator verifies: every request returns a diff or a justified no-op.

steps.title: Apply diffs
steps.description: Apply diffs in reverse line order per file, then rebuild. Coordinator verifies: zero orphan keys, zero undefined refs, citation density thresholds still met.

steps.title: Refresh Methods M.5/M.6
steps.description: Re-render the M.6 and M.5 phase outcomes from the final host.frames ledger. Coordinator verifies: the Methods ledger matches the recorded phase outcomes.

steps.title: Push to AllenNeuralDynamics/ComputationalReviewSSTdisease
steps.description: git clone https://github.com/AllenNeuralDynamics/ComputationalReviewSSTdisease, copy all outputs in, commit, and git push. Never use the Contents API. Coordinator verifies (Phase 20V): remote HEAD contains all files, hygiene scans clean.

steps.title: Post-deployment UX gate
steps.description: Run the tier-A static checks against the built Pages-artifact tarball. Run the tier-B live-URL checks, or produce a manual checklist if the sandbox cannot reach the deploy URL. Coordinator verifies: all tier-A checks pass; tier-B results or the checklist are recorded.
